issue_context.title: Add '--constraints'  flag to 'uv tool run'
issue_context.body:
The `--constraints` flag was recently added to `uv tool install` via #9547.  It would be really useful to add a similar flag to `uv tool run`. 
This would allow specifying version constraints for tooling in one place.  For example, 

```python
uvx --constraints tool-constraints.txt ruff
uvx --constraints tool-constraints.txt codespell
...
```

Thank you for this amazing package!

review_comments: I don't know if this is a good change. Previously, we just checked if the _environment_ was compatible with the request. Now, we check if the _receipt_ contained the exact same requested dependencies. This is consistent with `uv tool install`, but it's also "stricter".
@zanieb -- Did you have an opinion on this? Or too hard to say without more context?
I didn't think about it too hard, but I think it's basically okay. What motivates the change?
We can't use `satisfies` with `overrides`, so we'd need to two branches.
Hm, why can' we use `satisfies` with `overrides`? Aren't they just equivalent to constraints w.r.t. environments?
No, but we had an extensive conversation about this in the past... I'd have to dig it up.

I'll look at it separately. The current API definitely doesn't support it though and I think I determined that it was non-trivial when we tried in the past. (Note that everywhere that we use `satisfies`, we skip if `overrides` is non-empty.)
